analysis:
Integration pass over all 13 units. The PR changes only CI/advisory threat-review tooling: test scripts (.github/scripts/test-threat-*.py), scanner modules (threat-model-review.py runtime_seconds, threat_review/bedrock.py workload call policy and plan_calls, budget_runner.py, budget_scan.py, diagnostics.py), the threat-model-review.yml workflow, and docs. No provider runtime, coordinator WebSocket contract, key custody, attestation/App Attest, prefix cache (T-041) or fan-helper code is touched, so canonical assets A-001..A-017 and boundaries TB-002/003/007/009/010/011 are unaffected.

Security-relevant changes appear to tighten or preserve controls. The workflow_dispatch pr_number path is removed, so manual dispatch reaches only the unpaid preflight. THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA comes only from the pull_request payload. Manual job reruns (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT != 1) are refused before any paid work and hand off to a human. The workload Bedrock policy is capped at 100 calls with invalid values rejected, and unplanned calls hit a zero limit and fail closed. Fallback is restricted to explicit unavailable codes. Incomplete scans never produce clean(); the tests assert this for errors, uncovered units, pending depth, limited files and missing integration. The scan timeout is bounded 60..3000s and sits below the 60-minute job timeout.

Coverage limits: the integration replay was partial (60 of the source units omitted), and the workflow YAML, the budget_runner/budget_scan callers, merge_policy.clean and the metrics() content were seen only through patch excerpts and the earlier analyses, not verified end to end. The tests and docs assert behavior that I cannot confirm matches the full implementation. The open questions are cost and availability concerns, not provider-threat-model regressions. No finding is supported.
